newsitem.title: GERMANY: German grain harvest still dragging on-farm union.
newsitem.headline: German grain harvest still dragging on-farm union.

text.p: Changeable weather means the 1996 grain harvest is still incomplete and some winter sowings could be delayed, the German farm union DBV said on Wednesday.

The eastern German states of Saxony and Thuringia were hardest hit and while progress in other regions was already a month behind last year, higher-elevation areas in the two states had not even started cutting winter wheat.
The DBV said in a statement moisture content of 18-20 percent, compared with the 14.5 percent standard, as well as weight and quality losses were characteristic of such regions.
National volume forecasts were left unchanged at 41 million tonnes (39.9 million in 1995), but yields should vary widely.
The DBV estimated average western German grain yields six percent above last year's 6.1 tonnes per hectare, while eastern Germany's may be down 10 percent.
But spring barley volumes were up by 45 percent from last year's 1.85 million tonnes and yields should be 21 percent above the 4.3 tonnes per hectare seen in 1995.
Breadmaking and malting qualities were satisfactory across the board although frequent rain had hampered harvesting.
There was no shortage of wheat or rye for milling.
